description: Silicon-carbide crucible: an SIC vessel holding an AL61 metal charge ready to be melted.
name: sic_crucible
why: SiC sublimes/decomposes only around 2700 C, comfortably above the melting point of any metal charge you would put in it, and conducts heat fast and evenly (120 W/mK) into the melt; its PROP_CONDUCTS also reflects SiC's real use as a wide-bandgap power-semiconductor material outside of crucible service. Pair this with a jacketed HEAC/WIFI element beneath (see the insulated_heat_source practice) to actually melt the charge -- do not let AERO or other insulation touch the outside if the heating method needs direct thermal contact with the crucible wall.
